### Problem: Longest increasing subsequence II {#sec-lis-p4-lis2}

::: {.p-statement}
Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of `nums` whose consecutive values differ by at most `k`.

$1 \le n \le 10^5$, $1 \le nums[i] \le 10^5$, $1 \le k \le 10^5$. On $[4, 2, 1, 4, 3, 4, 5, 8, 15]$ with $k = 3$ the answer is 5: $1, 3, 4, 5, 8$. The step to 15 is 7, which is illegal. A plain LIS has length 6. On $[7, 4, 5, 1, 8, 12, 4, 7]$ with $k = 5$ the answer is 4. On $[1, 5]$ with $k = 1$ the answer is 1.

Source: [LC 2407 · Longest Increasing Subsequence II](https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-increasing-subsequence-ii/){.solved difficulty="Hard"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
The predecessor of $a[i]$ is an earlier value in $[a[i] - k,\ a[i] - 1]$. That is a window on the value axis, not a prefix, so the tails array cannot see it: tails answers "any smaller value", and here a much smaller value is illegal. A segment tree of the best length at each value answers the window in $O(\log A)$.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
- **State.** $dp[i]$ = longest legal increasing subsequence ending at $i$.
- **Transition.** $dp[i] = 1 + \max\{dp[j] : j < i,\ a[i] - k \le a[j] \le a[i] - 1\}$.
- **Structure.** A segment tree over values $1..10^5$ stores that maximum. Query $[a[i] - k,\ a[i] - 1]$, then write $dp[i]$ at position $a[i]$.
- **Answer.** $\max_i dp[i]$.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Why the tails array accepts an illegal step"}
The ordinary LIS of $[4, 2, 1, 4, 3, 4, 5, 8, 15]$ can end $1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 15$. The last step is $+7$. The constraint is on consecutive chosen values, so 15 does not extend 8 when $k = 3$, and it also does not extend anything else in range. The length is 5. A Fenwick prefix would have the same bug as tails: it would see every smaller value, including those more than $k$ below.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
`f(i)` is the best legal chain ending at `i`. The earlier index `j` is legal when the positive difference is at most `k`. The answer is the best ending.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("lis2", "rec")
    assert str(final) == "5"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: lis2-rec
def lis2_rec(a, k):
    def f(i):
        best = 1
        for j in range(i):
            if 0 < a[i] - a[j] <= k:
                best = max(best, 1 + f(j))
        return best
    return max(f(i) for i in range(len(a)))
```

##### C++

```cpp
int lis2Rec(int i, int k, const vector<int>& a) {
    int best = 1;
    for (int j = 0; j < i; ++j)
        if (a[j] < a[i] && a[i] - a[j] <= k) best = max(best, 1 + lis2Rec(j, k, a));
    return best;
}
```
:::

#### Memo

::: {.form-next}
`n` endings, each scanning earlier indices. Store `f(i)`. This is the $O(n^2)$ solution. It is correct, and it is too slow at $n = 10^5$.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("lis2", "memo")
    assert str(final) == "5"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: lis2-memo
def lis2_memo(a, k):
    memo = [-1] * len(a)

    def f(i):
        if memo[i] < 0:
            best = 1
            for j in range(i):
                if 0 < a[i] - a[j] <= k:
                    best = max(best, 1 + f(j))
            memo[i] = best
        return memo[i]

    return max(f(i) for i in range(len(a)))
```

##### C++

```cpp
int lis2Memo(int i, int k, const vector<int>& a, vector<int>& memo) {
    if (memo[i] >= 0) return memo[i];
    int best = 1;
    for (int j = 0; j < i; ++j)
        if (a[j] < a[i] && a[i] - a[j] <= k) best = max(best, 1 + lis2Memo(j, k, a, memo));
    return memo[i] = best;
}
```
:::

#### Table

::: {.form-next}
The same scan, written as a row. Equals do not extend: the difference must be positive. A difference larger than `k` is ignored even when the value is smaller.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("lis2", "tab")
    assert str(final) == "5"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: lis2-tab
def lis2_tab(a, k):
    dp = [1] * len(a)
    for i in range(len(a)):
        for j in range(i):
            if 0 < a[i] - a[j] <= k:
                dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + 1)
    return max(dp)
```

##### C++

```cpp
int lis2Tab(const vector<int>& a, int k) {
    int n = a.size(), ans = 1;
    vector<int> dp(n, 1);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        for (int j = 0; j < i; ++j)
            if (a[j] < a[i] && a[i] - a[j] <= k) dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + 1);
        ans = max(ans, dp[i]);
    }
    return ans;
}
```
:::

#### Segment tree

::: {.form-next}
Index the tree by the value. At `x`, read the maximum on `[x - k, x - 1]`, add one, and store it at `x`. A later equal value reads only up to `x - 1`, so it does not extend the earlier copy. The window is empty when nothing smaller is in range, and the length stays 1.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("lis2", "tree")
    assert str(final) == "5"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: lis2-tree
def lis2_tree(a, k):
    size = 1
    while size < max(a) + 2:
        size *= 2
    tree = [0] * (2 * size)

    def qry(lo, hi):
        if lo > hi:
            return 0
        ans, lo, hi = 0, lo + size, hi + size
        while lo <= hi:
            if lo & 1:
                ans = max(ans, tree[lo])
                lo += 1
            if not hi & 1:
                ans = max(ans, tree[hi])
                hi -= 1
            lo //= 2
            hi //= 2
        return ans

    def upd(i, val):
        i += size
        tree[i] = max(tree[i], val)
        i //= 2
        while i:
            tree[i] = max(tree[2 * i], tree[2 * i + 1])
            i //= 2

    ans = 1
    for x in a:
        got = qry(max(1, x - k), x - 1) + 1
        upd(x, got)
        ans = max(ans, got)
    return ans

one, k = [4, 2, 1, 4, 3, 4, 5, 8, 15], 3
assert lis2_rec(one, k) == lis2_memo(one, k) == lis2_tab(one, k) == lis2_tree(one, k) == 5
assert lis2_tab([7, 4, 5, 1, 8, 12, 4, 7], 5) == lis2_tree([7, 4, 5, 1, 8, 12, 4, 7], 5) == 4
assert lis2_tree([1, 5], 1) == 1
```

##### C++

```cpp
int lis2Tree(const vector<int>& a, int k) {
    int size = 1;
    while (size < 100002) size *= 2;
    vector<int> tree(2 * size);
    auto qry = [&](int lo, int hi) {
        if (lo > hi) return 0;
        int ans = 0;
        for (lo += size, hi += size; lo <= hi; lo /= 2, hi /= 2) {
            if (lo & 1) ans = max(ans, tree[lo++]);
            if (!(hi & 1)) ans = max(ans, tree[hi--]);
        }
        return ans;
    };
    auto upd = [&](int i, int val) {
        tree[i += size] = max(tree[i], val);
        while (i > 1) { i /= 2; tree[i] = max(tree[2 * i], tree[2 * i + 1]); }
    };
    int ans = 1;
    for (int x : a) {
        int got = qry(max(1, x - k), x - 1) + 1;
        upd(x, got);
        ans = max(ans, got);
    }
    return ans;
}
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Recursion**, **memoisation**, and the **table** are $O(n^2)$. The **segment tree** is $O(n \log A)$ with $A \le 10^5$. The values are already in $1..10^5$, so they do not need compression: the window endpoints are numeric. Compressing them would move $x - k$ off the rank axis.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- $k = 1$ and two values that differ by 2 or more: the answer is 1.
- A repeated value does not extend itself. The query stops at $x - 1$.
- Every consecutive step already at most $k$: the answer equals the ordinary LIS.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Running the tails array and then checking the printed subsequence. Tails optimises a different look-back. An illegal last step can sit in the ordinary LIS.
- Updating the tree before the query. The value would extend a chain that already ends at itself.
- A Fenwick prefix maximum. The discarded values are the ones below $x - k$, and a prefix cannot express a left endpoint.
:::

**Variants.** Adjacent letters at most $k$ apart in the alphabet is the same window on 26 letters, and an array is enough: [LC 2370 · Longest Ideal Subsequence](https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-ideal-subsequence/){difficulty="Medium"}. A weighted increasing chain of flower heights is a prefix maximum, so a Fenwick tree: [AC dp_q · Flowers](https://atcoder.jp/contests/dp/tasks/dp_q). $b_i = a_i - i$ turns a balanced subsequence into a maximum-sum non-decreasing subsequence: [LC 2926 · Maximum Balanced Subsequence Sum](https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-balanced-subsequence-sum/){difficulty="Hard"}.
